title: mruby Array#sort! uses the captured backing-store base after a comparison block shrinks the array, so a same-address realloc leaves it reading the trimmed tail
object: the Array's heap backing store (struct RArray as.heap.ptr), from mrb_realloc
lifetime_ender: ary_shrink_capa's mrb_realloc to a smaller capacity, which may return the same address
shape: a base pointer captured before a shrinking realloc, used after it past the new size
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: mruby's default allocf is libc realloc/free (src/allocf.c), a direct allocation with no GC slab or pool between it and the request
nested_why: the array backing store comes straight from mrb_realloc -> libc realloc, not from mruby's GC object arena
fidelity: allocator-level reduction: the capture, the shrinking realloc and the stale read are mruby's own, as a standalone case.c; it does NOT reproduce the VM path to sort_cmp. The measured instrument is probe.c / probe-capstone.c, scenario mruby-sort-bang-shrink
live_proof: fix eb398971b (2025-10-27, #6649) is an ancestor of mruby 4.0.0-rc2 (9d523e2f74f2), checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor, so the defect is fixed in that pin; src/array.c:2134 at the pin carries `RARRAY_PTR(ary) != p || RARRAY_LEN(ary) != n`. This case reconstructs the pre-fix allocator shape
distinguishing: the realloc SHRINKS and may keep its address, so unlike the FFmpeg move-and-rebase realloc cases (ffmpeg/plain-temporal-repros 02, 03) the defect does not need the block to move; the pre-fix guard was pointer-equality, so the same-address branch is exactly where it lived

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: stock CheriBSD purecap, the old backing-store capability read at the old index after the shrinking realloc. A SIGPROT is a catch; completion is the stale capability still usable.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD riscv64-purecap, one boot 2026-10-27; abi/bounds/revocation controls PASSED in the same boot
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: revocation on: the shim's shrink shortcut keeps the address with the full 512 B bounds, old tag set, the read completes (0x5a). revocation off: jemalloc moves (different size classes) but the old capability still reads its block. Silent under both layers.

virtual-malloc.oracle: Capstone virtual profile (musl mallocng behind runtime/virtual/heap.c, publish() revokes the old child on every realloc): a fault at the labelled read is a catch.
virtual-malloc.platform: p13, flat v7 gate platform (platform-sdev) with the dev control SDK runtime (heap-v6/sdk-control); fixed completed and freed faulted in the same run
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: revoked-capability fault at the READ label (pc minus code base 0x10730), cursor = old base + 504, old child's 512 B bounds; the block moved under our musl and still faulted
